transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Chen (KiteWorks Head of Platform), Devon Blake (KiteWorks SRE), Priya Rao (KiteWorks Security Lead)

Summary: Quick intake to understand KiteWorks expected call volume, latency targets, and security/residency constraints. Primary focus on per-token economics, batching and caching levers, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes sense given their compliance and latency needs.

Topics: cost/unit economics, batching impact, KV/prefix cache, residency/KMS, pilot scope and timeline

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: okay everyone, thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through, like, 30 to 45 minutes, gather your constraints and then outline next steps. Samir, wanna intro quick?
[00:12] Samir Patel: yeah hi all, Samir here, I'm the solutions engineer on the inference side, I'll focus on performance and benching. quick note — i'll ask a few clarifying q's about sample payloads.
[00:20] Maria Chen: great thanks. we pulled Devon and Priya because this is cross-functional — platform and security. we have a rough target: around 1.1B tokens/mo in Q1 if things go well, with bursts to 100 qps. latency target is 200 to 300 ms p95 for our chat LLM path.
[00:38] Devon Blake: and to be clear we have a hybrid setup now, some inference on prem for PHI, but most traffic is cloud. evaluating whether Redwood Hosted is acceptable or if we need Dedicated or Private for residency.
[00:50] Priya Rao: our security checklist: SOC2 is a must, SSO/SAML, KMS integration or HSM with customer keys, and audit logs with retention 1 year. also interested in egress minimization.
[01:05] Lena Ortiz: good, that's helpful — we support SOC2 and SSO, and KMS integrations in Private and Dedicated; hosted can also meet some of the KMS needs via customer-managed keys, but there are nuance, Samir can expand.
[01:18] Samir Patel: yeah so quick framing on cost: hosted off-the-shelf has per-token pricing and is easiest to start. Dedicated shifts to reserved GPU pools so you trade per-token for predictable throughput and lower marginal cost. Private adds the operational overhead but gives you the full KMS/HSM and vpc isolation.
[01:36] Maria Chen: rough question — how different are the per-token numbers? like, are we talking 2x, 3x difference?
[01:42] Lena Ortiz: it depends on workload and batching. typical delta is hosted is highest per-token, Dedicated has lower per-token at committed levels because of reserved capacity and better packing, Private can be similar to Dedicated when amortized but you add platform fees.
[01:55] Samir Patel: to add specifics — for a 70B-class model at our typical quant profile, if you're doing micro-batching for low latency, hosted might be ~X tokens/cent (placeholder), Dedicated with 8:1 batching improvement could reduce cost per token by 30–50% depending on utilization. obviously these are estimates, we should run your real prompts.
[02:14] Devon Blake: micro-batching? like how does that interact with p95 latency — if we batch too much we kill the latency tail.
[02:20] Samir Patel: exactly — there's a tradeoff. Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and dynamic sizing; you can set SLOs and a max batch window. for your 200–300ms p95 target we'd probably keep batch windows small (5–15ms) and rely on kv caching for repeated prefixes to reduce compute.
[02:38] Maria Chen: caching — tell me more. our users have many repeated openings and a lot of instruction-tuning, is prefix caching realistic?
[02:45] Samir Patel: yes, prefix/KV cache removes token compute for repeated context. in practice if you have high prefix reuse, you can see 20–60% token compute savings. Redwood also has a physical cache layer for hot keys in Dedicated/Private. hosted also caches but less customer-vis because of multi-tenant constraints.
[03:02] Priya Rao: that caching sounds good but how do we control residency of the cached data —does it store in our VPC?
[03:09] Samir Patel: in Private, yes — cache lives in your environment. Dedicated offers options: private pools that can be in a customer-specific tenancy. hosted keeps cache in Redwood-managed infra but we encrypt at rest and can apply residency controls per region. we'll detail that in the security doc.
[03:26] Maria Chen: a practical question — we've got an existing batching gateway that pre-aggregates requests, should we rip that out or layer Redwood on top?
[03:33] Samir Patel: usually we integrate. if your gateway does batching we can absorb it, but we recommend using Redwood's batching knobs because they have visibility into KV hits. if you keep external batching you might double-batch which can be inefficient.
[03:47] Devon Blake: for pilot scope, i think we want a hosted eval first to validate quality, then maybe a Dedicated pilot to test economics. timeline: Q4 pilot start?
[03:55] Lena Ortiz: that's a common path. hosted for quick quality check and then Dedicated for cost validation. for Q4 start we'd want to lock scope and sample prompts this month.
[04:06] Maria Chen: do you have examples of how batching impacts cost on real prompts? we've seen vendors hammer with theoretical numbers that don't reflect our long-turn conversation prompts.
[04:16] Samir Patel: good call — long-turn dialogues reduce batching efficiency per-token because sequence lengths get long. but KV caching is more effective there because earlier tokens in the session become cached. we'd like a set of sample conversations to run against our bench to show realistic per-token deltas.
[04:34] Speaker 1: sorry, who did you say runs the bench?
[04:36] Samir Patel: Redwood will run bench — we'll provide scripts, you run in your env for Private, or we run in Dedicated/Hosted environments for comparatives.
[04:44] Priya Rao: what about encryption keys — can we use our KMS? we have AWS KMS with key rotation policies.
[04:50] Lena Ortiz: yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys with rotation. hosted supports bring-your-own-key in certain regions — we'll include the exact limitations in the sheet.
[04:59] Maria Chen: any notes on throttling and fallback? we have to guarantee service if model spiky — can Redwood route to cheaper model when capacity is tight?
[05:06] Samir Patel: yes, smart routing — policy-based fallback to compatible variants. you can set cost-based or latency-based routing. for example, route to a quantized variant in Dedicated if primary is overloaded.
[05:18] Devon Blake: pkt loss and ephemeral failures during bursts — how do you preserve latency SLOs?
[05:23] Samir Patel: we do autoscaling within Dedicated pools up to burst capacity; also we recommend circuit-breaker and backpressure in the gateway. in Hosted we have multi-region fallback.
[05:33] Maria Chen: ok security again — audit logs, we need to export to our SIEM.
[05:37] Lena Ortiz: audit logs are supported across plans; in Private you get raw log export to your SIEM. Dedicated has forwarding. Hosted can ship aggregated audit artifacts, depending on plan.
[05:48] Priya Rao: does Redwood persist logs containing user PII? we have strict rules.
[05:52] Samir Patel: by default we avoid persisting user content in Hosted beyond short retention for debugging, but in Private you control retention. we'll include retention options in security doc.
[06:03] Maria Chen: who else needs to be involved on our side — legal? procurement?
[06:07] Devon Blake: procurement for any Dedicated contract, yes — legal will review pilot terms as well.
[06:12] Lena Ortiz: ok noted. next, let's talk about numbers — Maria you said 1.1B tokens/month — can you break down reads vs writes, average sequence lengths, and how many unique sessions?
[06:24] Maria Chen: rough split 70% chat (multi-turn, avg sequence 600 tokens), 30% batch embedding/semantic tasks (avg 120 tokens). unique sessions are high — many low-repeat end users but enterprise customers have repeat flows.
[06:38] Samir Patel: with those numbers, embeddings are more batchable and cheaper per token; chat will be the cost driver, but KV caching could significantly cut compute on repeated session starts. We'll model three scenarios in the pricing sheet: no cache, moderate reuse, high reuse.
[06:55] Maria Chen: what's the expected per-token swing between no-cache and high-reuse?
[06:58] Samir Patel: ballpark 1.8x to 3x depending on model size and prefix reuse. again, sample prompts will sharpen that.
[07:08] Devon Blake: any minimums for Dedicated? we don't want to overcommit if usage fluctuates.
[07:12] Lena Ortiz: Dedicated typically has a reserved minimum for GPU pools; we can structure tranche ramping — start smaller and add capacity. we'll propose a flexible commit in the terms.
[07:23] Maria Chen: ok — what about instrumentation — do we get token-level cost and latency breakdown for routes and tokens?
[07:29] Samir Patel: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency per model/route, token histograms, and trace linking to requests. that's how you find hot prompts.
[07:40] Speaker 2: also, the console shows KV hit rates which is helpful for detecting caching opportunities.
[07:45] Priya Rao: small question — does Redwood's runtime require specific model formats? we plan to use an open LLM we trained.
[07:52] Samir Patel: we support common formats (HF, GGUF, ONNX in many cases). for custom models we have onboarding assistance; sometimes small conversion steps are needed.
[08:03] Maria Chen: last part — price transparency. we need detailed line items for per-call, per-token, storage, cache, and reserved capacity.
[08:12] Lena Ortiz: absolutely. I'll include a line-itemized pricing scenario and a worked example for your 1.1B token profile across the three hosting modes.
[08:21] Devon Blake: can you include run-rate examples showing break-even point between Hosted and Dedicated? like thresholds where Dedicated becomes cheaper?
[08:28] Samir Patel: yes we'll include threshold analysis and sensitivity to caching and batching.
[08:33] Maria Chen: okay that's helpful. timeline again — pricing sheet this wk, perf plan next, pilot run last week of Sept/first of Oct?
[08:43] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. we'll aim to get the pricing to you by 2026-09-17. Samir will follow up with perf scripts and a proposal for the bench.
[08:51] Priya Rao: and I will send our compliance matrix by EOD next Tue.
[08:57] Lena Ortiz: perfect. quick recap of next steps — send pricing, security docs, bench plan, schedule bench. any other blockers?
[09:05] Maria Chen: none from me. thanks all.
[09:08] Samir Patel: thanks, we'll be in touch.
[09:12] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: minor speaker-attribution glitches early on (Speaker 1/2), occasional filler and run-ons captured, proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., KMS vendor names omitted).
